subject: ent
title: Oral, oropharyngeal and hypopharyngeal cancers

steps.tx: **Oral cavity cancer** (lip, tongue anterior two thirds, floor of mouth, buccal, palate, gingiva) is mostly squamous carcinoma driven by tobacco, alcohol synergy and betel or areca nut (submucous fibrosis), presenting as non healing ulcer over three weeks, red white patch (erythroplakia highest risk, leukoplakia), induration, loose tooth or referred otalgia. Oral tongue and floor metastasise early to levels I to III; depth of invasion now stages and drives elective neck treatment thresholds.
steps.say: Mouth ulcer three weeks is cancer until biopsy proves kind. Red patches outrank white for danger.

steps.tx: **Oropharyngeal cancer** split biologically: HPV positive (tonsil, tongue base, younger, cystic nodes, better prognosis, p16 marker) versus tobacco alcohol HPV negative (worse response). Hypopharyngeal cancer (pyriform sinus commonest subsite) presents latest and worst: dysphagia, odynophagia, referred otalgia, hoarseness from laryngeal invasion, weight loss and nodes, often with second primaries from field cancerisation of upper aerodigestive tract in smokers and drinkers (synchronous lung or oesophagus vigilance, panendoscopy traditions).
steps.say: HPV throat cancer answers treatment better. Pyriform sinus cancer arrives late and behaves worst.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Assessment maps primary (examination under anaesthesia, biopsy, p16), neck (ultrasound guided node sampling, CT or MRI, PET for advanced or unknown primary), distant spread (chest imaging) and host (nutrition, teeth, speech swallow, smoking alcohol cessation, anaesthetic). Unknown primary with squamous neck node triggers tonsillectomy and tongue base sampling pathways plus EBV and p16 testing to localise nasopharynx versus oropharynx origins.
steps.say: Node without primary: test p16 and EBV, take tonsils and tongue base samples.

vis.alt: Sagittal diagram showing head and neck anatomy, highlighting common cancer sites in the oral cavity, oropharynx, and hypopharynx, and associated neck lymph node regions.
vis.caption: Anatomical subsites of head and neck cancers

steps.tx: **Key point.** Treatment is multidisciplinary by stage: early oral cancers surgery with margins and sentinel or elective neck dissection, reconstruction free flaps for tongue and floor defects; advanced or oropharyngeal often chemoradiation preserving organs, with surgery salvage. Hypopharynx frequently needs combined modality and laryngectomy decisions balancing voice. Dental clearance before radiation prevents osteoradionecrosis; speech, swallow and gastrostomy planning and smoking cessation change survival as much as modality choice.
steps.say: Cut early mouth cancers, beam many throat cancers, save voice where oncology allows. Teeth out before radiation or jaw bone dies.
